title: Question: are images adored properly or only improperly? Some older Scholastics say only improperly
source_text: XXXIX. His ita observatis quaeritur in Schola Romana An Imagines sint proprie adorandae, an vero solum improprie? Et fuerunt inter veteres Scholasticos nonnulli qui fatentur quidem imagines aliquo modo adorandas esse, & licitum esse eas osculari, & coram iis procumbere, & circa illas alia honoris signa exercere, non tamen per hoc imagines proprie, sed improprie tantum & abusive adorari: quia, scilicet, actiones illae, quanquam circa imagines fiant, non tamen fiunt in honorem imaginum, sed in honorem prototypi, nec imagines sunt terminus ad quem refertur illa adoratio.
pass_a_gloss: These things having been thus observed, it is asked in the Roman School whether Images are to be adored properly, or truly only improperly? And there were among the older Scholastics some who grant indeed that images are in some way to be adored, and that it is lawful to kiss them, and to prostrate before them, and to exercise other signs of honor around them, yet not thereby that images are properly adored, but only improperly and abusively: because, namely, those actions, although they happen around images, yet are not done unto the honor of the images, but unto the honor of the prototype, nor are the images the terminus to which that adoration is referred.
pass_b_english: Roman School question: proper or only improper adoration of images?
Some older Scholastics allow kiss, prostration, and honor-signs, yet call that adoration improper or abusive—acts toward images terminate on the prototype, not the image.

lemmas.gloss: the terminus to which it is referred

choices.why: Technical School sense, not moral abuse alone.
